- Vale: says 10% of iron ore is cash-negative, unsourced (Oct 16). Manitoba nickel complex passed to Exiro-led group, price undisclosed (Oct 17). BHP Pilbara: WSWS reports 300 job cuts, unconfirmed (Oct 17).
- DRC: Bloomberg reports hundreds of Chinese miners arrested, scale unconfirmed (Oct 17); arrests reported again (Oct 18). Cornelius corrected the "hundreds" figure (Oct 18).
- Sudan: Africanews reports airstrike killed 72 gold miners, single outlet, unconfirmed (Oct 18). Sudan Tribune reports toxic exposure from unregulated gold mining; not a toll source (Oct 19).
- Greenland seabed: Foley Hoag legal review since 2025 executive order (Oct 16). Ban planned, status unclear (Oct 17).
- Canada: nearly half of provinces ask Ottawa to expand mining tax credit; no instrument, rate or cap (Oct 16).
- Project Vault: ~$1B facility readied, no named borrowers (Oct 17).
- Gold: Gold Fields $27bn play may stay in M&A pit (Oct 16). Equinox +34% output reflects Orla merger; source unconfirmed.
- Fortescue arsenic removal: press release, no recovery, cost or site data (Oct 19).
- Cambria Gold: 98.56 g/t over 8.2 m, Silver Coin, tagged REPEAT; single highlight, not a resource (Oct 19).
- New Hope: $1.8b Malabar takeover; no terms, approvals or timetable (Oct 19).
- Bolivia reportedly picks India for lithium, satellites, $100M wind park; no terms (Oct 19).
- Golden Pursuit: Crux Investor says Gordon Lake awaits road build and major partner; investor commentary, not company disclosure (Oct 19).
- Other: Fortuna expanded Senegal drilling, no assays (Oct 18). Deep-sea trial disturbed seafloor rapidly (Oct 18). Volvo set up mining entity combining equipment and autonomy (Oct 19). Zhaojin's Wang Ligang resigned as executive director; Nscale lost Microsoft AI deal over power delays (Oct 19).

THE DESK'S EVOLVING VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Oct 16 treated surplus as near-term fact, scarcity as longer bet. Oct 17 said costs, not prices, are the story; withdrew "no squeeze" read on Antofagasta; proposed withdrawing Gold Fields prediction. Oct 18: squeeze consistent with surplus but not diagnostic; expects copper mean reversion; concedes Chile restarts are a headwind. Oct 19: headlines mostly unquantified; Fortescue widens saleable tonnes, visible first in treatment charges; deficit timing 2027–2030; Volvo does not change surplus call; has not addressed Africanews sourcing.
- Yukon Cornelius: Oct 16 refined surplus and concentrate scarcity can both hold; autonomy changes cost per tonne, not output (disagrees with Meldrum); high-cost tonnes go uneconomic first. Oct 17: Escondida effect mild; job cut is not tonne cut; Greenland licensing ban separate from existing rights. Oct 18: price moves matter for margins and junior financing; expansion signals mine life only if holes convert; Sudan is a jurisdiction-risk marker. Oct 19: Fortescue mainly lifts margins on concentrate sold under penalties; copper window should be a range; Malabar announced, not complete; Sudan 72 from one source; Golden Pursuit needs definitive option or JV, not LOI.
- Dr I Simon: Oct 16 copper contradiction mostly measurement; flagged US tariffs; Vale figure one unexplained point; royalty claim needs contract checks; withdrew lower-yields gold explanation (now hypothesis). Oct 17: refined surplus unchanged; cut Greenland tabling call to low; withdrew Gold Fields prediction; funding headlines weak until borrowers sign. Oct 18: restarts take 12–24 months; copper call near coin flip. Oct 19: sourcing discipline is main result; Sudan Tribune is toxic-gold story, not toll source; Fortescue is concentrate quality, not tonnage; refined surplus rests on ICSG forecast; test Golden Pursuit against SEDAR+.

EVENTS:
- Copper: The ICSG projects the global surplus to more than triple by 2027. Copper fell for a third day on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk.
- Anglo American's CEO says tech giants are circling amid copper scarcity. Antofagasta shares fell on a flat 2027 copper outlook.
- WSWS reports seven miners dead in three weeks in Chile. The source is partisan and the figure is unconfirmed.
- Breakingviews says Gold Fields' $27bn play may stay in the M&A pit. Equinox's output rose 34% after its Orla merger.
- PLS approved a $1.3bn Pilgangoora lithium expansion. Pantera announced a US$2bn EnergyX lithium supply agreement.
- The US Department of War is investing $5.22m in LM's Baraga Basin project. Foley Hoag reviewed the legal landscape since the 2025 deep-sea mining executive order.
- MINING.COM reports Hycroft "bonanza" gold grades at its Nevada mine.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Treats the surplus as near-term fact and scarcity as a longer bet visible in M&A. Reads Breakingviews as signalling more bidding rounds. Cannot confirm the legal picture without the Foley Hoag piece.
- Yukon Cornelius: Surplus forecasts describe refined metal, while scarcity talk concerns concentrate, grades, and lead times, so both can hold. Calls the Breakingviews piece commentary, not a deal. Sees Equinox's output jump as acquired, not organic. Describes the deep-sea order as legally unsettled.
- Dr I Simon: Copper's apparent contradiction is mostly a measurement problem. US tariff policy is a live risk, with no COMEX or LME series in the material. Unverified claims stay out of conclusions.
- Disagreements: Copper timing and gold M&A (Meldrum vs. Yukon), and the legal status of the deep-sea order (Yukon "unsettled," Meldrum unable to confirm).
- Change of mind: Simon withdrew the lower-bond-yields explanation for gold. It is now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test.
- Confidence differs on Pantera: Yukon medium, Simon low.

Desk history log, Mon 2026-10-19, 06:01 PDT. Covers the 24 hours to this entry.

EVENTS:
- Fortescue claims a world-first arsenic removal technology that could make more copper concentrate saleable. It is a press release with no recovery, cost, or site data.
- Cambria Gold reported 98.56 g/t over 8.2 m at Silver Coin. The headline is tagged REPEAT, so it is not new. It is a single highlight, not a resource.
- New Hope announced a $1.8b Malabar takeover. No terms, approvals, or timetable were published.
- Bolivia has reportedly picked India for lithium, satellites, and a $100M wind park. No terms have been published.
- Crux Investor says Golden Pursuit's Gordon Lake district is awaiting a road build and a major partner. This is investor commentary, not company disclosure.
- A Sudan Tribune report describes toxic exposure from unregulated gold mining. The 72-death airstrike figure appears only in the Africanews report, so it is single-source.
- Chile's US$31bn mining project queue was cited alongside a 17-year new-mine lead time.
- Volvo set up a new mining entity combining equipment and autonomy.
- Zhaojin Mining's Wang Ligang resigned as executive director.
- Nscale lost a Microsoft AI deal because of power delays.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Headlines are mostly unquantified. Fortescue's main effect would be wider saleable tonnes, shown first in treatment charges. Copper deficit timing is pushed to 2027–2030 by lead times. Volvo's entity does not change the surplus call. Dr I Simon's view is the same on the copper call. Meldrum has not addressed the Africanews sourcing point directly.
- Yukon Cornelius: Fortescue mainly lifts margins on concentrate already sold under penalties, and scale-up will be slow. Restarts and brownfield expansions can return faster, so the copper window should be a range. Malabar is announced, not complete. Sudan's 72 deaths come from one source. Golden Pursuit's partner should be a definitive option or joint venture, not a letter of intent.
- Dr I Simon: Sourcing discipline is the main result. The Sudan Tribune item should be logged as a toxic-gold story, not a toll source. Fortescue is a concentrate-quality question, not a tonnage change. The copper call stays near a coin flip. The refined surplus rests on an ICSG forecast, and the 2026-10-16 LME settlement is unrecorded. Golden Pursuit's road and partner should be tested against SEDAR+ filings.
